newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries mired in London, mood cautious pre-data. [CORRECTED 10:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Treasuries mired in London, mood cautious pre-data. [CORRECTED 10:55 GMT]

text.p: U.S. Treasuries traded in London were cowering on the sidelines ahead of a week of key economic data, traders said on Monday.
But in the very short term, they still have limited upside potential as expectations remain that U.S. interest rates are on hold for the time being -- and amid a dearth of data this session.

"Business is fairly slack, with prices kept tight in a range by profit-taking on one side and dip-buying on the other," said a trader at a U.S. bank in London. "It needs to get tomorrow's data out of the way."
The U.S. 30-year long bond was trading at 102-07, yielding 6.458 percent compared with 102-04 in Tokyo and 102-07 in New York.
September T-bond futures were down 2/32 in automated trade at 114-31.
On Tuesday, the second quarter employment cost index was scheduled for release at 1230 GMT, followed by real GDP on Thursday, and monthly non-farm payrolls data on Friday.

"If you wish to remain bullish on Treasuries, then you have to have to expect that interest rates will be cut, at least in 1998," said Teis Knuthsen, international economist at First Chicago in London. "If you don't think that then it's hard to justify being bullish."

He said he was forecasting growth in the U.S. accelerating in the third quarter, and that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates as soon as Autumn (corrects from August) to counteract that. The Federal funds rate currently stands at 5.50 percent, after a quarter-point rise in March.

But rather than a sell-off, Knuthsen said Treasuries were likely to be subject to steady erosion -- and higher-than-expected economic data would have a more pointed effect on the market than any figure which comes in below forecasts.
At the short end, December Eurodollars were down 0.005 at 94.12.
